items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: And during that time our friend Alec Wilder entered the scene.

ctx.x: Because we could also move there. He had his own club, it was called Charlie’s — what was it called? Open House. And it was on the White Horse Pike outside of Philadelphia, and so it was sort of a semi-permanent thing. We worked there every weekend and he would bring in a comedian from New York City and put on a show and it was a big sort of a white elephant club out on the highway. It was a great place. It had a great stage and a great dance floor, so it was a fun place people came out to. He did very well there…

And during that time our friend Alec Wilder entered the scene. We met him through a friend. We were working in New York City. And this friend of ours, who is Rogers Brackett, who is in advertising, said, “listen, I’d like Alec Wilder to hear you, because you’re doing some wonderful things now.” And he said, “could you come to this apartment, it’s on Central Park South?” Okay, sure. So we walk in and here’s this sumptuous apartment overlooking Central Park, and here’s a little piano over there and pictures on it…
Oh, no, oh, no. Which was his sign of approval.
